text:
olivia: Heads-up — saw a 3.2x spike in audit events between 21:10-21:25 UTC last night. Ingest queue spiked and customers saw intermittent 503s. Suspect a change in admin tooling + KMS calls. Anyone already digging?

sam: saw the alert in SRE channel. queue depth hit ~22k, shards started rejecting bulk writes.

ingest-bot: ALERT: audit-ingest-queue length=22134, write_errors=540, avg-bulk-ms=420

natalie: Do we have a schema change rollout around that time? I didn't touch audit schema but several teams pushed RBAC helper scripts yesterday.

ryan: @natalie checking deploy history now. quick grep shows a new `rbac-actor-attrs` field started being emitted by admin-service at 21:08 UTC. Could increase event size + KMS envelope calls.

olivia: if admin-service starts adding nested attrs, ES bulk sizes jump and indexing cost goes up. Also KMS per-event envelope encryption can blow up latency if synchronous.

sam: confirmed: admin-service PR merged 2026-03-14 20:58 and rollout finished ~21:05. It added `actor.attrs` with ~200-400 bytes per event on average.

natalie: that explains size bump. but why the write_errors? should be backpressure from our ingest pipeline.

sec-eng-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: INC-2026-045 - audit-ingest backpressure impacting hosted customers (severity: P2)

ryan: pipeline metrics show batching contigs reduced (smaller batch counts but larger payloads). ES bulk timeout hit and we started returning 429/503 upstream.

olivia: suspects list: 1) RBAC change increased payload size, 2) synchronous KMS envelope calls in admin-service for certain operations, 3) no sampling on admin event stream.

sam: immediate mitigation options we can do now: 1) temporarily enable sampling for `admin:*` events at ingress 2) increase ingest broker workers 3) enable async KMS envelope (if feasible) 4) short-term reindex throttle on ES.

natalie: for customer-facing validation we need to be careful — sampling may hide audit coverage for customers who rely on 1:1 retention. Need to notify enterprise customers and offer opt-out or guaranteed route.

ryan: agree. we should add a live flag on a per-tenant basis: `audit_sampling_rate` default 1.0 for enterprise with contract, 0.1 for free tier. quick toggle via console.

olivia: for the long term: add size-aware batching and backpressure policy. e.g., instead of N events per batch, use byte-limit + event-count cap. Also KV-cache-style prefix dedupe for repeated actor.attrs to reduce redundancy.

sam: here's a snippet we can try in broker config to limit batch bytes and fall back to immediate flush at X ms:

```yaml
audit_ingest:
  batch_max_events: 1000
  batch_max_bytes: 4MB
  batch_max_delay_ms: 100
  backpressure_threshold: 15000
```

natalie: also need to confirm KMS integration pattern. If admin-service calls KMS per event to wrap key, that's expensive. We should switch to batching envelopes or client-side wrapping with a local cache of DEKs.

ryan: quick experiment: disable synchronous KMS wrap in staging and run replay. Should we toggle `USE_KMS_SYNC=false` for admin-service canary?

olivia: do it but only in canary tenants. @sam can you schedule a canary rollback if it worsens? :thumbsup:

sam: will do. Also opening a quick PR to add tenant-level sampling toggle in console.

ingest-bot: NOTE: Created runbook task RB-752 to add batch_max_bytes and sampling flag.

natalie: action items I'm taking: 1) draft customer notice about potential sampling and how to request full retention 2) audit schema PR to make `actor.attrs` optional and size-bounded 3) add validation to the producer library to cap per-field bytes.

ryan: my action items: 1) implement batch-bytes in broker 2) add metric `batch_bytes` and `avg_event_bytes` 3) prototype DEK cache for envelope wrapping.

olivia: timeline: do canary KMS async test + broker batch-bytes change in next 6 hours, revert if errors. natalie to send customer notice draft within 12 hours. If mitigation holds, we'll roll to prod and open an RFC for schema + SLAs for audit retention.

sam: one more thing — indexing cost. ES mappings for `actor.attrs` as `text` with full analysis is expensive. Set to `keyword` or a small `text` with index=false for free-tier to save cost.

natalie: good call. I'll matrix which fields need full-text vs exact-match. Also recommend a policy: large nested objects should be stored in object blob and not indexed by default.

olivia: thanks team. let's sync again in 2 hours after canary test. tagging @ryan @sam @natalie.

ryan: on it.

sam: canary toggled, monitoring. linking dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/ingest/audit-ingest-overview

ingest-bot: UPDATE: canary queue depth stable at 420, avg-bulk-ms=85

natalie: draft notice: "We experienced elevated audit ingest latency affecting a subset of hosts. We've enacted temporary sampling for non-contract tenants and will work with enterprise customers to ensure full coverage. Root cause: a schema addition increased per-event size and triggered downstream bulk timeouts." Posting for review.

olivia: looks good; add contact for SOC and customer success.

sec-eng-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED: INC-2026-045 -> mitigated (canary stable). Next step: postmortem + schema gating RFC.

olivia: assigning postmortem owner: @natalie — please include cost delta estimate for last 24h and recommended schema guardrails.

natalie: noted. I'll put together a short postmortem and RFC by EOD.

ryan: will include perf graphs and batch-bytes patch in PR.

sam: closing loop with SRE on scaling options and emergency capacity.

olivia: thanks everyone :heart:
